claims.text: Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles begin surface premelting earlier than comparable binary or single-element nanoparticles.
Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu HEA nanoparticles have a more broadly distributed premelting onset than comparable binary or single-element nanoparticles.
High configurational entropy produces heterogeneous local bonding environments in HEA nanoparticles.
Heterogeneous local bonding environments and strain fields lower local melting barriers.
The starting Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles are initially solid and single-phase.
The starting Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu nanoparticles have a homogeneous elemental distribution.
Cooling rate can affect retention or formation of the single-phase HEA solid solution.
Local fluctuations in elemental identity and atomic size induce surface-structure variation and lattice strain.
Randomly distributed metal atoms with different sizes and cohesive energies create heterogeneous bonding environments.
Local regions of reduced cohesive energy initiate surface disordering at lower temperatures.
Limited atomic mobility broadens the temperature range over which premelting begins.
A high degree of lattice strain broadens the temperature range over which premelting begins.
Simpler binary nanoparticles have more uniform bonding that delays and sharpens melting.
Relative to size-matched Fe–Ni nanoparticles, the HEA nanoparticles will display surface disorder and lattice softening at slightly lower temperatures.
Relative to size-matched Fe–Ni nanoparticles, the HEA nanoparticles will display a broader premelting interval before complete melting.
The proposed mechanism applies to single-phase HEA nanoparticles in the 3–10 nm size range.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to bulk materials or to nanoparticles with significant elemental segregation or oxidation.
Particle-size distribution and surface effects can influence the premelting-onset shift and premelting-range broadening.
Failure to observe either a statistically significant lower onset temperature or a broader premelting interval relative to the binary control would falsify the hypothesis.
